**Group:** Other  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A silicoflagellate: the cell contains an internal siliceous skeleton built from a basal ring with radiating spines, often looking like an open star. The living cell is a single flagellate with many small golden-brown chloroplasts around the skeleton. Key features: geometric open silica skeleton with spines (not a solid frustule), single cell.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **centric** | Diatoms have a solid, box-like silica frustule; Dictyocha's silica is an open latticed skeleton of a ring plus spines, not a pillbox valve. |
| **heterosigma** | Heterosigma is a naked flagellate with no silica; Dictyocha has a rigid internal silica skeleton. |
